solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Female hit boyfriend? One's seen to be fiery

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit hard
a beau is a boyfriend or admirer

explanation.surface: A woman lashes out at her boyfriend and is seen to have a fiery temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hangs on 'boyfriend', but the definition is the last part: a flaming torch is something seen to be fiery.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaming torch carried at night is literally a burning light, so it is a thing seen to be on fire.

clue.text: March forward to restrict a hunt

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the forward march encloses the a

parts.note: to forge ahead is to march forward

explanation.surface: Troops advance to put limits on a hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to restrict' puts A inside FORGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To search widely for food or supplies is to hunt about for them.

clue.text: Colleagues in gatherings after leader has been deposed

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: rallies are mass gatherings

explanation.surface: Fellow members meeting up once their leader has been ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after leader has been deposed' removes the R from RALLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Partners or associates working on the same side are colleagues.

clue.text: Effrontery in support given to heartless deception

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: heartless says the central letter of the word for deception is removed

parts.note: a cheat is a deception or swindle

explanation.surface: Cheeky insolence that backs up a cruel fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle E from CHEAT, leaving CHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent answering back is a form of cheek or insolence.

clue.text: Affected person quietly drifting away

indicators.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quietly, and it drifts off

parts.note: party means a person, as in the guilty party

explanation.surface: A pretentious person slipping quietly out of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quietly drifting away' removes P (piano, quiet) from PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentiously artistic is affected in manner.

clue.text: Enlargement of hostelry seen as retrograde — vulgar interior

indicators.note: interior tells us the vulgar word sits inside the reversed hostelry
retrograde means moving backwards, so the word for the hostelry is read in reverse

parts.note: a pub is a hostelry
low means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the pub extension has been done backwards, with a tasteless interior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen as retrograde' reads the hostelry backwards, giving BUP; 'interior' means the vulgar word goes inside, not an adjective about the decor.
explanation.definitionFit: In photography a big print made from a small negative is called by this name, meaning an enlarged copy.

clue.text: Archbishop when meeting Her Majesty becomes a comedian

indicators.note: meeting says the two pieces join side by side

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An archbishop meets the Queen and turns into a clown.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Harry Lauder was a Scottish music-hall entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish music-hall star known for songs and jokes was a comic performer.

clue.text: Poet needs to be more funny — that's an extra aspiration

indicators.note: an extra letter is added to the word, slotted inside

parts.note: wittier means funnier
H represents an aspirate, a breathy sound

explanation.surface: A poet aspiring to be funnier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's an extra' adds H (an aspirate) inside WITTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: John Greenleaf of that name was a nineteenth-century American poet.

clue.text: Very good food for one to tuck into? It's wretched

parts.note: pi is short for pious, very good

indicators.note: tuck into means go inside, so the one goes into the food

parts.note: table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Pious food for someone to tuck into is miserable fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tuck into' places I inside TABLE, after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserving pity, so pathetic or miserable.

clue.text: Move firm to the west — get special advisory service round

indicators.note: round says the counselling service wraps around the reversed firm

parts.note: Relate is the British relationship counselling charity

indicators.note: in an across clue, going to the west means reading right to left, so the firm is reversed

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A business thinks of shifting westward and calling in consultants to help.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'to the west' means read leftwards, giving OC; Relate is the UK marriage guidance charity, which 'round' wraps about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift premises or home to a different place is to move.

clue.text: Queen isn't whimsical

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A short verdict that the monarch is not given to flights of fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something oddly charming and old-fashioned, appealingly fanciful.

clue.text: Old ruler's down, up in dance

parts.note: a czar was a Russian emperor

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: sad means down, depressed

explanation.surface: An old ruler is depressed, then cheered up by dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SAD to DAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hungarian folk dance that starts slowly and speeds up.

clue.text: Endlessly flourishing church in the country

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter of the word for flourishing is cut off

parts.note: green means fresh and flourishing, like young growth
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church that never stops flourishing somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like it modifies flourishing, but it cuts the last letter, leaving GREE; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hellenic Republic in south-east Europe is a nation state.

clue.text: Paper shows one garment, one found in South Africa

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: found in says the garment and the second one sit inside the abbreviation for South Africa

parts.note: ZA is the international vehicle and internet code for South Africa
a vest is a garment
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a single item of clothing turning up in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: ZA, the internet code for South Africa, is the container: 'found in' places the garment and the second 'one' within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian daily newspaper of that name, once the Soviet government organ, is a paper.

clue.text: African city making offer in the course of a month

indicators.note: in the course of means within, so the offer goes inside

parts.note: Jan is short for January
a bid is an offer

explanation.surface: An African city making a bid during a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the course of' means during, so the offer sits inside the month with its article attached.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief city and port of Ivory Coast is in West Africa.

clue.text: City's coarse food on the turn

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is a city

parts.note: ham means crude or clumsy, as in ham-fisted or a ham actor

indicators.note: on the turn says the word for food is turned around

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: A city's rough food is going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the turn' suggests food going sour, but it reverses GRUB to BURG.
explanation.definitionFit: The German port on the Elbe is a major city.

clue.text: PM as Lord after change of direction

indicators.note: the R for right is changed to L for left, a change of direction

parts.note: a peer is a lord

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister becoming a Lord after a political U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after change of direction' swaps R (right) for L (left) in PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Robert of that name, founder of the modern police, was a British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Officer and politician (a Leftie) set side by side

parts.note: CO is a Commanding Officer
MP is a Member of Parliament
a red is a left-wing person

explanation.surface: An officer and a left-wing politician placed next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things beside each other for comparison is to set them side by side.

clue.text: Stains produced by insects, dreadful being embedded

indicators.note: embedded means set inside, so the dreadful word is lodged in the insects

parts.note: bees are insects
grim means dreadful

explanation.surface: Insects leaving dreadful marks behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being embedded' signals that the dreadful word is lodged within the insects; 'produced by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dirty with ingrained soot or grime is to soil or stain.

clue.text: This strangely gripping old TV series seen as a big success

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so the mixed-up letters close around the series
strangely means the letters of the word are mixed up

parts.note: M*A*S*H was a long-running American TV comedy

explanation.surface: An oddly gripping old television show becoming a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' scrambles This into S plus HIT, and 'gripping' has those letters hold the Korean War sitcom between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely popular record, show or film is a big success.

clue.text: Old governor making one toe the line

parts.note: a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned ruler forcing someone into line.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe the line is an idiom for doing as one is told, conforming to the rules.

clue.text: Unrighteousness makes girl looking two ways hurt inside

indicators.note: inside says the word for hurt goes into the girl's name
the girl's name reads the same forwards and backwards, so it looks both ways

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
harm means hurt

explanation.surface: A two-faced girl with an inner hurt is behaving wickedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking two ways' marks the girl's name as a palindrome, reading the same both ways; 'inside' puts the hurt within it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu thought the term is the opposite of dharma, meaning wrongdoing or lack of virtue.

clue.text: Animal is excellent, without disease

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the excellent letters surround the disease

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI
gout is a disease of the joints

explanation.surface: An animal declared excellent and free of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here it is the old sense of outside: the excellent letters surround the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American rodent related to the guinea pig is an animal.

clue.text: Gentleman admitting affection, nothing less for the old folk?

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the gentleman takes in the reduced affection

parts.note: sir is a title for a gentleman

indicators.note: O is nothing, and it is removed

parts.note: love is affection

explanation.surface: A gentleman showing affection, minus nothing, to the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing less' drops O from LOVE to leave LVE, which SIR is 'admitting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey hair suggests age, so the colour is used for things aimed at older people, as in silver surfers.

clue.text: Good weapon making oblique movement

parts.note: a lance is a weapon

explanation.surface: A fine weapon making a slanting move.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow or ball that strikes at an angle and deflects makes a sideways, slanting move.

clue.text: Soldier, fellow to defend a country

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: to defend is to surround protectively, so the fellow wraps around the a

parts.note: guy means a fellow

explanation.surface: A soldier and his comrade called up to defend a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to defend' means to stand around and shield, so the fellow encloses the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlocked South American republic with Asunción as capital is a nation.

clue.text: Slip back over island to make observation

indicators.note: the reversed slip is placed over the island letter, enclosing it
back says the word for slip is read in reverse

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or minor error

explanation.surface: Someone slips back across an island to keep watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LAPSE into ESPAL; I goes inside it, which 'over' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic noun for spying or catching sight of something, so a noticing or watching.

clue.text: This Irish singer will be seen in a commercial coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: a commercial is an ad, so the phrase gives an ad

explanation.surface: An Irish singer appearing in an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses AN AD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish singer who won Eurovision in 1970 performed under that single name.

clue.text: Disturbance as drink after drink gets knocked back

indicators.note: after places the second, reversed drink behind the first

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: knocked back hints at downing a drink but here means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A row breaks out as one drink after another is knocked back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets knocked back' sounds like drinking but turns the second drink around, giving PUS, which 'after' places second.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy commotion or uproar is a disturbance.

clue.text: What quiet Axminster offers as a place for dodgy financiers?

definitions.text: What quiet Axminster offers as a place for dodgy financiers?

parts.words: What quiet Axminster offers as a place for dodgy financiers?
parts.note: the run of letters at the join of quiet and Axminster spells a levy, and a quiet market town is a refuge

explanation.surface: Wondering what a sleepy Devon town could offer shady money men.
explanation.walkthrough: Axminster is a small market town in Devon. The first part sits at the join of 'quieT AXminster', and a quiet town is a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Offshore jurisdictions with minimal levies attract those seeking to shelter their money.

clue.text: One animal to suffer when impeded by fool

indicators.note: being impeded by something means having it stuck in the middle, so the fool goes inside

parts.note: to die can mean to suffer, as in dying of embarrassment
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An animal suffering because a fool gets in its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when impeded by' means the fool blocks the middle of the suffering verb; the animal is the South African rock hyrax.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African name for the rock hyrax, a small furry mammal, so it is one kind of beast.

clue.text: Bird dunked in wet dressing, not cold wine

indicators.note: dunked in says the bird is plunged into the dressing
C is the abbreviation for cold, found on taps, and is taken away

parts.note: a sauce is a liquid dressing for food
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird dunked in wet dressing, served with wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not cold' drops C, the tap abbreviation, from the dressing, leaving SAUE; 'dunked in' plunges the bird into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white dessert wine from the Bordeaux region of France.
